note: Phase 7 (plans/phase-7-deployment.md), written 2026-11-13 by the session that will write the reader, from the files of each clone at its pinned commit (read by hand, with a scratch script listing compose services and what their images lead to). A reviewer subagent with a fresh context went over every entry against the clones on 2026-11-13 (all citations held; it added the nkp chart's CloudNativePG database and corrected a count), but the reader's author still wrote the file, so read the score generously. A frame is a file (or a chart or Terraform folder) that runs something (decision 2), named by its path. `step` is the plan's step that should first draw it (1: compose, charts and Terraform declaring a resource on the map; 2: a compose file whose only news is a service tied to code; 3: Procfiles, systemd units, plain Kubernetes manifests, compose files found by content). A service `runs` either a `resource` (an id as the resources scorer names it, `sql` for any SQL database) or `code`: the folders it runs, as a careful person reading the files would say (`.` is the whole workspace). A drawn tie is right when every folder is covered by a box at or inside it and no box falls outside them. `rung` is the first rung of decision 3 that reaches the service (1 `build:`, 2 the Dockerfile's own names, 3 a command named as a declared start, null none), and `by` the lines it rests on. A service with `untied: true` names only an image (rung 4): any tie drawn for it is wrong, even one that happens to match. `optional` services and frames are neither required nor counted as extra. `mustNotAppear` are frames that are wrong to draw (tests, devcontainers, fixtures, files R2 already draws); `outOfScope` are formats the plan leaves for later, counted as extra if drawn. Plain services (a proxy, an admin tool) are not scored.
